steps.title: Distance is not the cause
steps.say: Yes — Earth is actually farthest from the Sun in early July, during northern summer. So distance alone cannot explain the heat.

ops.text:
Northern summer: Earth is FARTHER
from the Sun in early July.

steps.title: What the tilt does
steps.say: The tilt changes how directly sunlight hits the northern hemisphere. In June it leans toward the Sun, so the same sunlight is concentrated over a smaller area.

ops.text:
Tilt changes how DIRECTLY sunlight hits us.
Direct light = more energy on each square meter.

steps.title: June: northern hemisphere leans in
steps.say: In June the northern half of Earth leans toward the Sun, so sunlight strikes it more directly and days are longer.

ops.text:
June: N. hemisphere
tilts toward the Sun

steps.title: December: northern hemisphere leans away
steps.say: In December the northern half leans away, so the same sunlight spreads over a larger area and days are shorter.

ops.text:
December: N. hemisphere
tilts away from the Sun

steps.title: Direct vs slanted sunlight
steps.say: The same beam of sunlight is concentrated when it hits straight on, and spread out when it hits at a slant. That is why tilt matters more than distance.

ops.text:
Same beam:
• direct hit = concentrated, hotter
• slanted hit = spread out, cooler
